items.content:
Dear Pathfinders,

To provide a better experience, Polaris Institute will continue to improve the game and address any issues identified. The fixes included in this update are as follows:

>>Bug Fixes

1. Fixed an issue where the active Aniimo had a small chance of failing to Revive properly after fainted multiple times in a Sanctum. If Pathfinders still encounter this issue, exiting and re-entering the current scene can fix.

2. Fixed an issue where Catch results could not be processed correctly.

3. Fixed an issue where the hatching conditions for "Bond Eggs" did not match their descriptions.

4. Fixed an issue where Pathfinder using non-ATK Skills would trigger Aniimo ATK.

5. Fixed an issue where Bloom in "Zephyrus Landbridge" were linked to the wrong Aniimo Family.

6. Fixed an issue where Shrubclaw could disappear during the cave activity in Argent Strait.

7. Fixed an issue where NPCs could disappear during interaction, preventing Pathfinders from proceeding.

8. Fixed an issue where Pathfinder voice lines could overlap.

9. Fixed an issue where "Daily Activity" mail rewards were displayed incorrectly when resent.

10. Fixed an issue where Accessory adjustments were not saved after swapping slots.

11. Fixed an issue where designated Aniimo were not refreshed after using Nurture Offerings to Nurture Veins in certain Areas.

12. Fixed an issue where hair could appear stretched during initial character customization.

>>Optimizations & Adjustments

1. Optimized the icons and descriptions of Held Items in "Elite Training".

2. Optimized the display of "Mark Sharing". When "Mark Sharing" is near other interactable targets, its entry will be automatically hidden from the interaction List. To interact with "Mark Sharing", move away from other interactable targets.

3. Adjusted rules displayed on "Aniimo Exchange".

items.title: Currency Guide: All Currencies and What to Save
items.summary: Aniimo is a game that has multiple types of currencies that you can earn as you play the game. These currencies give you access to certain rewards and special
items.content:
Aniimo is a game that has multiple types of currencies that you can earn as you play the game. These currencies give you access to certain rewards and special items, but it can be difficult to know what currencies do, how important they are, and which ones you should be saving up. We have you covered. Here's everything you need to know about every currency that you can find while playing Aniimo.

Here are the major currencies that you'll be trying to unlock and add to your character as you play through Aniimo.

There are a lot of currencies for you to collect and keep track of while you play Aniimo. Of the ones you want to collect the most is the Lumin Crystals, as they require real-world money to you to acquire and use, there are few, if any, chances for you to unlock them by playing the game.

You primarily want to keep track of Credits, Glimmer, Home Coins, Starwish Coins, Voxel Coins , and Windborn Stamps.

The Credits and Glimmer are readily available to you as you play the game, and are the standard currencies that you can acquire regularly by completing quests and story progression. Of the two, Glimmer is far more important, as you can use it at the in-game shop to purchase fruits, Aniipod Ultras, Redesign cards, or Primergy for in-game activities.

Home Coins are a currency you can get to unlock special furniture and items for your RV, making it a more distinct location for your home. You can get Starwish Coins by turning in your Voxel Coins at the Super Lucky Star vendor, and you can only get 1,000 Voxel Coins per week. You want to unlock at least 1,000 once per week to make sure you can maximize this limited currency.

Finally, the Windborn Stamps are available to you by completing various activities, and unlocking rewards in the Stamp Shop. These are limited to each season with Aniimon, and are important to redeem if you want those rewards for that season in the Companion Handbook.

items.content:
Dear Pathfinders,

Here is a summary of the currently known game issues. Polaris Institute is actively working to resolve them. Please take note of the following:

1. Some visual effects may display abnormally when entering Astra for the first time.

2. Some Pathfinders may experience a red screen display issue in-game. As a temporary workaround, try switching the graphics quality to Performance Mode in Settings. This issue is expected to be fixed in future updates.

>> Additional Information

If a black screen occurs, please try the following:

1. Update the graphics driver.

2. Try switching between DX11 and DX12.

3. Disable DLSS and Frame Generation on the login screen.

To provide a better experience, Polaris Institute will continue to improve the game and address any issues identified. The fixes included in this update are as follows:

>>Bug Fixes

1. Fixed an issue where some Pathfinders could experience a red screen display issue in-game.

2. Fixed an issue where characters' eyes appeared abnormally red on certain graphics cards.

3. Fixed issues with Quick Twine and multiple forms being unable to participate in the Susuta and Dr. Glass challenges.

4. Fixed an issue where item source text in the Stamp Shop was incorrect.

5.Fixed an issue where certain terrain could occasionally become impassable while collecting Butterfly Shadows during the Story quest "The Land Where Dreams Come True," preventing quest progress.

6. Fixed an issue where the button for the "Star Pop-Up, Spud Squad Assemble" event displayed abnormally when hovered over with the mouse.

7. Fixed an issue where text in some shared marks displayed abnormally.

8. Fixed an issue where Companion Handbook EXP was not displayed properly on the Monthly Pass make-up check-in reward screen.

9. Fixed an issue where some Home formulas had incorrect values.

10. Fixed an issue where crossover event decorations in Astra were floating in midair.

11. Fixed an issue where chimney wind fields in Nimbus Fields displayed abnormally.

12. Fixed an issue with incorrect asset references in quest cutscenes.

13. Fixed an issue where interface text overlapped in one location during the Story quest "Another Departure."

14. Fixed an issue where an objective description was incorrect during the Story quest "Another Departure."

15.Fixed an issue where the description of the Pathfinder's Aeroboard skill was inaccurate.

16. Fixed an issue where using Unstuck while interacting with a two-player mechanism in a two-player Sanctum could cause players to become stuck.

17. Fixed an issue with incorrect punctuation in the Mysterious Vendor's dialogue.

>>Optimizations & Adjustments

1. Changed "Auto Voice" to be disabled by default in the settings at the bottom left of the chat interface. You can enable it as needed.

2. Optimized the spawn rules for Prismana Aniimo. When a Lucky Strike fills Prismatic Energy to maximum, Prismana Aniimo in the area can now respawn immediately.

3. Adjusted the locations of some chests that could not be claimed.

4. Reduced the default number of marks shared by strangers displayed in Settings. For existing characters, this can be adjusted manually in Settings.

5. Changed the type of item consumed to evolve Squarrel.

6. Optimized the conditions for obtaining Tilling Chest.

7. Removed error notification mail for common Aniipods to reduce notification disruptions. The actual items returned are unaffected.

items.title: Free-to-play Creature Collector RPG Aniimo launches on PC, PlayStation, and Xbox
items.summary: Pawprint Studio has released creature collecting RPG, Aniimo, on PC (Steam, Epic), PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S.
items.content:
After months of beta testing, Pawprint Studio has released creature collecting RPG, Aniimo , on PC (Steam, Epic), PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. It’s also coming to mobile platforms on September 23.

Xbox Game Pass subscribers also receive an exclusive monthly Aniimo pack, which includes 1 Aniipod Ultra, 15 Growth Flowers, and 300 Glimmer.

Aniimo is a colorful world filled with creatures, inspired by Genshin Impact and Pokémon. As new Pathfinders, it’s the player’s job to explore the world of Idyll and discover the titular Aniimo.

At launch, the game includes over 200 Aniimo, including regional and color variants, and multiple rarities.

The open world features multiple territories supporting different levels of play, from quests to bosses and hidden treasures, and more.

In addition to summoning different Aniimo in real-time battle, players can also merge with their Aniimo directly. The process is called Twining, and it’s what sets Aniimo apart from most creature battlers. Through Twining, players become their favorite Aniimo, battling in third-person action. Each Aniimo has unique abilities and traits, and many can help travel around the world by gliding, climbing, or swimming.

Pathfinders also gain access to their own personal Homeland area, where they can build, expand, and customize an automated farm, and provide a home to their Aniimo.

I quite enjoyed the game when I played the Aniimo beta earlier this year.

Although primarily designed as an online single-player game (like many Hoyoverse gacha games ), Aniimo supports cooperative play to join with friends, or engage in specific PvP modes.

“The Aniimo team has worked diligently to finally bring the dreams of ourselves and our players to reality,” said Janson Zhang, Lead Game Designer, Pawprint Studio. “Through their efforts and immense support from Pathfinders around the globe, the world of Aniimo is now ready for you to discover with us, and we can’t wait to go on this journey together!”

Aniimo is free-to-play on PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. It releases on September 23 on iOS and Android mobile platforms. A Mac version is also coming soon. It’s rated E10+.

more ambitious with the launch of Aniimo , a free-to-play open-world RPG that lets you do more than simply capture and battle its colourful inhabitants.

Developed and published by Pawprint Studio, Aniimo is now available on Xbox Series X|S, PC and PlayStation 5, with Xbox Play Anywhere support included. The game is also available through Game Pass Day One across the Ultimate, Essential, Premium and PC tiers, while a mobile release is scheduled for September 23rd.

We first covered Aniimo back in 2025 , when its unusual Twining mechanic offered an early glimpse at how it planned to stand apart from other creature-collecting adventures.

Aniimo takes players to the expansive continent of Idyll, a world where creatures known as Aniimo can be found across a variety of environments. Their appearances and behaviours are influenced by factors such as weather, time of day and surrounding phenomena, giving exploration a purpose beyond simply travelling from one objective to the next.

Capturing these creatures requires a little more thought than pressing a button and moving on. Players can use Aniipods, set traps and carefully time their attempts, while the creatures themselves can evolve as their journey progresses.

The aim is to build a collection, but Aniimo also wants players to develop a connection with the creatures they discover.

The defining feature of Aniimo is its Twining system. Rather than simply sending a creature into battle, players can merge with their collected Aniimo and experience the world through their abilities and perspective.

This can open up new ways to approach puzzles, overcome obstacles and engage in battles. Depending on the creature involved, players may be able to glide, dive, burrow or use other skills to reach places that would otherwise remain inaccessible.

That makes the process of collecting Aniimo feel directly connected to exploration. Finding a new creature isn’t only about adding another entry to your collection – it could also provide the solution to a problem you’ve encountered elsewhere in Idyll.

Idyll isn’t intended to be explored entirely alone. Players can visit a floating metropolis, meet fellow Pathfinders and take part in competitive battles, while the PvEvP mode known as Egg Heist introduces a more immediate multiplayer challenge.

In Egg Heist, teams of three head into the Lost Isles to search, compete and battle in real time. The mode is designed to mix cooperation with uncertainty, ensuring that other players can complicate proceedings as you work towards your objective.

Outside of combat, each Pathfinder also has access to a personal RV parked at a campsite. This provides a place to interact with other players, while returning to Homeland allows you to plant crops, arrange decorations and customise your own space.

Aniimo is available now on Xbox Series X|S, PC and PlayStation 5, with Play Anywhere support on Xbox and PC thanks to the Xbox Store download. The mobile version follows on September 23rd.

Could this be the next Palworld to offer players an alternative to Pokémon?

Aniimo is a new open-world creature-catching RPG from Chinese developer Pawprint Studio. In the game, you explore a vast world and throw cubes at wild Aniimo to catch them before using the creatures in battle. Sounds a lot like Pokémon , right?

However, Aniimo puts its own spin on the familiar formula by allowing players to transform into their creatures. You can then directly control them to explore the world, complete traversal sections and solve puzzles.

Like Palworld , Aniimo appears to offer a fresh take on the catch ’em all genre. Despite only launching today, September 16, the game is already a hit on PC. According to SteamDB , Aniimo has surpassed 101,717 peak concurrent players on Steam . Considering it is still early morning across much of North America, that is pretty impressive!

It is difficult to say whether this will be the next Palworld , but Aniimo has already impressed Pokémon fans with its gorgeous visuals. However, despite its promising player count, not everyone is enjoying the new creature-catching RPG.

At the time of writing, Aniimo has a “Mixed” user rating on Steam. One of the biggest complaints is that the game reportedly adopts a gacha-like structure after its opening tutorial, with microtransactions and paid options that can speed up progression.

“Has such potential. Very good graphics, cool design of aniimo. However about an hour into the game you are bombarded with monthly passes, stores, objectives that you can bypass by paying, ways to speed up your levelling. Its very much a gatcha game,” one Steam user review reads. Another frustrated reviewer wrote: “Aniimo promised an authentic, gacha-free creature collector, but it delivers nothing more than a glorified digital storefront.”

It should be pointed out that the game does not require players to purchase these items. Not every review has been negative, either. One player wrote: “Im already loving how cute the aniimo and everything about this game is. It’s basically Palworld + Infinity Nikki! ”

While its Steam reviews are currently mixed, Aniimo is already off to a strong start based on how many people are playing it. Even if it does not reach the ridiculous heights of Palworld , this is another example of how much demand there is for new Pokémon-like games. And with Pokémon Winds and Waves still around a year and a half away, I totally get it.

The new free-to-play creature-catching RPG game runs smoothly out of the box, but getting that crisp, native 4K monitor look without your frame rate taking a hit means going in and adjusting a few things yourself.

If you've got a high-end gaming PC sitting around, you're in a great spot to see Aniimo at its best. Below, we've put together the settings that gave us the cleanest, most stable 4K experience on PC, along with a quick note on what to expect if you're playing on PS5 instead.

Aniimo isn't the most resource-demanding game out there. If you want to run it natively at 4K using the settings below, you'll want noticeably more GPU power than the minimum or recommended requirements call for.

This includes modern GPUs like the Nvidia GeForce RTX 4070, 4080, and 4090, alongside AMD cards like the Radeon RX 7800 XT and 7900 XTX. The settings below are designed to offer a fantastic balance between image quality and solid performance at 4K.

The display settings below aren't about maxing out every slider. After all, the world is full of creatures, particle effects, and dynamic lighting. So, I've picked a perfect mix that keeps the visuals sharp while leaving enough performance on the table for a steady FPS.

Here are the best 4K Video settings for Aniimo on a high-end PC:

Also Read: Aniimo PC benchmarks on Nvidia RTX 5070 Ti

DLSS or FSR Quality mode, depending on your GPU, is doing a lot of the heavy lifting here. It renders the game at a lower internal resolution and upscales the image back to 4K, clawing back a good chunk of performance without making things look soft. Keeping VSync off helps input lag stay low too, which matters even in a laid-back game like Aniimo.

DLSS Frame Generation lets you push the multiplier up to 6x or hand things over to Dynamic Mode. However, I have settled on 4x as the best balance, since going higher can introduce a bit of smearing around fast-moving creatures without adding much once your base frame rate is already solid. If you are using an extremely high refresh rate monitor and want the smoothest motion possible, try pushing it to 6x or testing Dynamic Mode to see how your setup feels.

You can keep all on High for Global Illumination, Reflection Quality, Ambient Occlusion, and Shadow Quality, since a high-end PC can handle real-time lighting without breaking a sweat. Bake Global Illumination is left off on purpose, as it swaps in a static, pre-computed lighting solution meant for lower-end GPUs.

Also Read: Aniimo not working on PS5: Possible fixes and reasons

Under the Other display settings, you set how busy Idyll should feel. Wild Aniimo Displayed, Pathfinder Aniimo Displayed, Other Pathfinders Displayed, and Scene Objects Displayed decide how many creatures, other players, and background objects show up around your in-game character at once. Sliding these to max would give you the most alive version of Idyll, but only if your hardware can handle the load.

As for Saturation, Brightness, and Contrast, these are purely down to your personal choice. If you notice some odd frame rate dips, the first things you should try are dialing down the Frame Generation multiplier and Shadow Quality. Those settings tend to give you the biggest performance return for the smallest visual cost.

With these settings, Aniimo would look impressive in 4K on a high-end PC. From the glow of a freshly hatched creature to the light bouncing off the floating city above Idyll, you would have the best visual experience while not sacrificing performance significantly for catching, battling, and exploring the new RPG world.

Aniimo is now available worldwide on Xbox Series X|S, Xbox PC, and Xbox Game Pass. Pawprint Studio’s creature-collecting game launches with more than 200 Aniimo for players to discover, meet, and collect across the world of Idyll.

That launch roster includes Squarrel and its evolution, Squashel, which are among the newest creatures added to the game.

One of the more substantial launch changes concerns Irisalis. Responding to beta feedback, the studio redesigned the Legendary Aniimo’s entire encounter flow, including its capture process, gameplay experience, and encounter ritual. This goes beyond a balance adjustment, revising how a major creature encounter unfolds from beginning to end.

Training has also been reworked for launch. The Held Item System has been simplified, Star Dust drop rates have increased, and progression caps now unlock alongside each Aniimo’s level progression. Taken together, those changes appear intended to reduce friction between collecting a creature and continuing to develop it.

Elsewhere, Pawprint Studio refined Homeland progression and upgrades while expanding its map with more features, activities, and interactive elements. Mobile and gamepad controls have been optimized, while multilingual voice acting has been added to the main story alongside improved translations.

The interesting detail here is that Irisalis is not a one-off revision. Pawprint Studio will use the redesigned encounter structure as the foundation for future Legendary Aniimo events, giving today’s launch update a direct line into the game’s next major creature encounters.

items.content:
The moment creature-collecting fans have been waiting for is finally here. The team here at Pawprint Studio is delighted to see Aniimo officially launch today, bringing the vibrant world of Idyll and its adorable creatures, the Aniimo, to players around the world. This is the chance for all of us to finally jump into the adventure, explore diverse regions, and discover the Aniimo who thrive across Idyll’s unique biomes.

First, we want to thank all the players who participated in our beta tests and shared feedback on gameplay, mechanics, and features. Your support and insights have helped us shape the game and reach the moment we have all been waiting for – global launch! I wanted to share with you how this feedback has contributed to the game’s development and what new additions you can expect to encounter!

At launch, players will be able to discover, meet, and collect more than 200 Aniimo. Among the newest additions are Squarrel and its evolution, Squashel. This energetic squirrel-like Aniimo rolls down hillsides while clutching its tail and attacks using fast-paced combo mechanics centered around its powerful tail abilities. It is a unique addition to the Aniimo roster and we think that players will have a lot of fun with it!

Following important feedback from our pioneering Pathfinders, we redesigned the entire Irisalis encounter flow across three key areas: capture, gameplay experience, and the encounter ritual itself. This updated structure will also serve as the foundation for future Legendary Aniimo events, creating a smoother and more intuitive experience for players. Again, we’re grateful for the feedback on this gameplay sequence which has had a profound impact on how we view these events.

We have also improved the way Pathfinders train and level up their Aniimo. Updates include a simplified Held Item System, increased Star Dust drop rates, and progression caps that now unlock naturally alongside an Aniimo’s level progression.

We refined the overall level progression and upgrade experience within Homeland gameplay, while also expanding the map with additional features, activities, and interactive elements for Pathfinders to explore and enjoy.

Additionally, we’ve optimized controls for both mobile devices and gamepads to deliver a smoother experience across all platforms. We’ve also added multilingual voice acting to the main storyline and improved translation quality across all supported languages, creating a more immersive and seamless gameplay experience for players worldwide.

These improvements are only the beginning. Our goal at Pawprint Studio is to create a fun and exciting creature-collecting experience that players can enjoy for years to come, and your feedback will continue to help shape the future of Aniimo . We are truly grateful for all the support and passion you have shown throughout every stage of bringing Aniimo to life.

Whether you are stepping into the world of Aniimo for the very first time or have been following our journey from the beginning, the gates to Idyll are finally opening. We’re excited to welcome you into this magical universe and invite you to become part of the adventure. Join us on XBOX Series X|S, XBOX PC, and XBOX Game Pass today.

For the latest updates on Aniimo , upcoming events, and future content, visit www.aniimo.com and follow our community channels . Join the community and continue your journey through the world of Idyll with fellow Pathfinders around the globe.

items.title: A Letter from the Aniimo Dev Team
items.summary: Hello everyone, we’re the development team behind Aniimo, Pawprint Studio. It’s been an honor, over the past year and beyond, to share Aniimo’s first reveal and the three tests that followed with all of you. From our first meeting to every
items.content:
Hello everyone, we’re the development team behind Aniimo, Pawprint Studio.

It’s been an honor, over the past year and beyond, to share Aniimo’s first reveal and the three tests that followed with all of you. From our first meeting to every encounter across each test, we’ve heard a lot of love, and plenty of honest frustration too. Thank you, truly, for taking the time to tell us what Aniimo looks like through your eyes, and for your support and patience all this way. Today, we’d like to make it official once more: Aniimo launches worldwide on PC, console, and Xbox cloud gaming on September 16, with the mobile version arriving September 23. We are all super stoked to finally get to meet you in Idyll!

Why Does Aniimo Exist?

Over the past year, one question has come up again and again from media and players alike: why make a game like Aniimo at all? The answer is actually pretty simple. Before we were developers, we were players. Like so many of you, we grew up on creature-collecting games, and we fell in love with the companions that stayed by our side through them. We’ve all trekked halfaway across game world just to meet one creature we adored. We’ve all had a chance encounter that kept us smiling for days. And somewhere in the back of our minds, one simple thought never quite went away: what if I didn’t just adventure with these creatures—what if I could really meet them, understand them, even become them, and see the world the way they do?

That thought became the seed for everything: a vast open-world adventure across Idyll, a story of exploration that takes you from the touch of a paw to the heart of the world. In the beginning, all we built was a world for the Aniimo to live in. But as we kept creating, ideas started springing up out of that world on their own. Their families, their quirks, how they got along with each other, all their odd little behaviors. Piece by piece, it all took shape. And sometimes, the strangest feeling would creep in: it didn’t feel like we were designing these Aniimo anymore. It felt like we were discovering them. The Emberpups who trail devotedly after their leader. The Nimbis drifting lazily over the grasslands. The Susutas who pile onto the beach to play in crowds. As each one came into focus, we’d catch ourselves thinking: of course. That’s exactly what they’re supposed to be like. That's why we love Aniimo.

The joy was never just in inventing creature after creature—it was in walking through a world like Idyll and finding them there, one step at a time. Stumbling onto a family you’d never met, an Aniimo you’d never seen. Noticing the funny relationships between them, realizing this world is so full of stories. That joy of discovery is what we want to pass on to you. We hope that when you set foot in Idyll, you’ll start with your own footsteps and eventually leave paw prints no one else could leave. And to everyone who’s ever dreamed of adventuring alongside creatures as wondrous as the Aniimo: Idyll is waiting, and so are the encounters meant for you.

The Core Experience of Aniimo

So what kind of game is Aniimo, really? For those of you about to set foot in Idyll for the first time, we’d like to take this chance to introduce the adventure that awaits you there.

Everyone who comes to Idyll becomes a "Pathfinder," gaining an incredibly unique ability. Because here, you don’t just have an Aniimo. You can become one. By establishing bonds and twining with Aniimo, you’ll not only fight at their side and unravel the world’s mysteries, you’ll also actually join their families, and come to know the stories playing out between them. And most importantly, you can step into an Aniimo’s point of view—seeing the whole continent again through their eyes, their wings, their senses.

All across Idyll, countless Aniimo of every form, temperament, and habit live freely, each with their own families and their own way of life. When you meet them, we hope you’ll see more than something to put in the index. We hope you’ll see a life that actually belongs here. That’s why the journey at the heart of Aniimo was never about grinding stages and ticking off a checklist. It’s about walking into a living, breathing world and writing your own stories alongside the creatures who call it home.

Where does the journey end? That’s an answer we’d rather leave to each Pathfinder. Perhaps you’ll become the professor who’s cataloged every Aniimo, or perhaps the undisputed champion of Aniimo battles. Perhaps you’ll become Idyll’s greatest treasure hunter, a master gardener, a home design genius... How you play and who you become are entirely up to you. Our story begins the moment palm meets paw print.

Your Words Genuinely Changed Aniimo

From the very first sketches of Idyll, we wanted Aniimo to be an adventure we finished together with our players. Every test has been a chance for us to see the game with new eyes, for you to discover new content and systems, and for us to take a hard look at what we’d built.

When the most recent test wrapped up, we went through everything carefully: the praise and the anticipation, and the blunt, unsparing criticism too. We want the changes themselves to prove a point: what you said didn’t just sit in forums, group chats, and feedback forms. Here’s some of what has already landed in the launch version.

  • The Irisalis Catching Experience

    [/*]

In earlier tests, many Pathfinders who met Irisalis told us the same story: throwing ball after ball got dull fast, and stacking the entry cost and repeated throws on top of pure luck turned a legendary encounter into a draining chore. Looking back, we saw the problem clearly. We’d hoped randomness would make meeting a Legendary Aniimo feel like a challenge—but we’d overlooked some players’ experiences, and this repetitiveness made the experience less immersive of what we set out to create.

For launch, we’ve redesigned the entire process of obtaining Irisalis around three things: how you reach it, how it plays, and how the encounter itself feels. This design will be the template for every Legendary Aniimo encounter to come.

How you reach it: No more repeating the challenge in the hope of a successful catch. Collect legendary tokens through world exploration and story progress, craft your own personal Legendary Aniipod, and unlock Irisalis’s exclusive story.

How it plays: Token collecting is incorporated into everyday exploration and catching, so progress builds naturally as you adventure.

How the encounter feels: Once your Legendary Aniipod is crafted, the exclusive encounter appears on the map. Enter the battle, follow the story, defeat the Legendary Aniimo, and throw the Aniipod you made to seal your bond with Irisalis. This encounter only happens once, so make it count.

  • Changes to Acquiring and Encountering Prismana Aniimo

    [/*]

The base chance of triggering Prismana Aniimo through nurturing is now flat, removing the early-game probability decay from low Prismatic Energy (every nurturing now has the same chance of triggering Prismana Flow). The guarantee system remains.

A new lucky strike mechanic has been added to catching. Lucky strikes grant item rewards, increase the area’s Prismatic Energy, and have a chance to directly trigger Prismana Flow, attracting Prismana Aniimo.

Wild Surges triggered through ecosystem nurturing now offer a chance to encounter Umbral Aniimo, who have Perfect Potential and distinctive coloration. Umbral Aniimo can also be encountered by chance in the open world.

Offering quality no longer affects Wild Surge quality. Ecosystem nurturing now grants a fixed amount of Prismatic Energy.

Spawn rules for season-exclusive Prismana Aniimo have been reworked, with clearer, more intuitive trigger conditions.

  • Easier Aniimo Training

    [/*]

The Carried Item system has been simplified: random rune slots are gone, and the rune system has been removed entirely.

Legendary Star Dust output has been increased. Capability Awakening for Aniimo below Lv. 60 can now be reset at any time, with the training items returned.

Capability caps now unlock gradually with Aniimo level and Resonance star rank, easing early progression pressure.

Capafruit effects now transfer automatically between Aniimo during inheritance, so switching which Aniimo you raise no longer requires the same investment all over again.

  • Home Improvements

    [/*]

The RV upgrade experience has been improved, with adjusted upgrade times to ease resource shortages after upgrades.

The Home has expanded into a multi-area map with house building and a large selection of new furniture. Interior decorating will continue to be improved.

Order refresh logic has been improved, with more order variety.

Furniture groups can now be shared via codes, and multi-select limits have been raised.

New interactive furniture has been added, and some pieces can now be placed and used out in the open world.

Home Aniimo have new idle AI behaviors, improved work logic, and a new petting interaction.

Unused furniture can be sold back at a discount through the Co-op Store.

RV dispatches now have a chance to produce Aniimo eggs with the Prismana trait.

New Home season events offer season-exclusive furniture and formulas.

New soil-tilling social interaction: till the soil at another Pathfinder’s Home to earn a share of their harvest.

  • Other Improvements

    [/*]

Improved controls on mobile devices and with controllers.

Multi-language voiceover added to the main story, with improved translation quality across all languages.

Aniimo caught with a Sparkling Cube now have guaranteed Perfect Potential.

Operation: Egg Heist has been substantially improved, with more obtainable egg types and a new high-difficulty Chaos Mode. PvP event modes will continue to be refined.

Spawn rates for high-Potential 9/9 and 10/10 wild Aniimo have been increased.

Journey quest guidance has been rebuilt, fixing vague requirements and progression blockers.

New Pathfinder Challenge rematches, plus AI teammate support for Holo-Battle Interlink.

The player character’s look has been refined, alongside improved NPC models, animations, and expressions.

A New Invitation

Through every test, you’ve spoken up. And whether it came as criticism or encouragement, every word you’ve shared has been precious to us. In what you’ve told us, we’ve come to see your standards for quality, your love and support for Aniimo, as well as your doubts and disappointments. So in the days ahead, we hope you’ll keep telling us what you think and what you hope for. If Aniimo is going to become a genuinely great game, it can’t be built on the dev team’s judgment alone. To help Aniimo thrive, we need to work together with everyone who loves the game. We hope Aniimo becomes more than a game to you. We hope it becomes a way of life you can truly look forward to.

Thank you all.

Aniimo shines brighter because of you, Pathfinders!

May we meet in Idyll.

Pawprint Studio

Ahead of Aniimo’s launch, 2026
